title: Reference origin depths had a larger shallow-share rise than centroid depths in 3,734 matched earthquakes in 2005-2020
abstract: We split a reported depth-class change gap for 3,734 matched earthquakes in 2005-2020 into two terms. At depth 15 km or less, shallow share rose by 5.39 percentage points in ComCat origin depths, 6.22 points in Global CMT reference origin depths, and 0.18 points in centroid depths. The ComCat-to-centroid change gap of 5.20 points equals -0.84 points between origin fields plus 6.04 points between reference origin and centroid. Conditional 95% three-year block limits for the latter term were 2.87 to 9.01 points. Strict 15 km and inclusive 20 and 30 km cuts retained a positive reference-to-centroid term. A FREE-only check was uncertain. Thus, the difference between current preferred ComCat depth and stored reference origin depth does not produce the positive gap. This is a catalog diagnostic, not proof of physical shallowing or a revision cause. Short eras, shared errors, event clustering and source changes limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, an independent matching audit and repeat checks are supplied. Source records remain external.

display.caption: The same matched events have three depth classifiers. The late-minus-early ComCat-to-centroid change gap splits into origin-to-origin and reference-to-centroid terms. Error bars are conditional 95% three-year block limits.

citations.reason: Extends its matched-event comparison with a third depth field and an exact change split. Same shared raw snapshots; new code.
GCMT boundary sensitivity motivates starting after 2004.
